title: Disk access time and disk schedulers
brief: Compute seek, rotation, and transfer time for a hard disk, then order a queue of track requests with FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, and C-LOOK.
hints: One full rotation takes 60000 / rpm milliseconds. On average the target sector is half a rotation away, so average rotational latency is half of that.
Transfer time is bytes divided by bytes per second. Convert megabytes per second to bytes per second with 1,000,000 bytes per megabyte, then multiply by 1000 for milliseconds.
For SSTF, pick min(pending, key=...) with a key of (distance, track). Ties go to the lower track, so the track belongs in the key. Remove one copy of the request with list.remove.

For SCAN going up, split the queue into tracks >= start and tracks < start. Sort the first ascending. If the second is not empty, add max_track to the path unless the head already ends there, then add the second sorted descending.
C-LOOK never turns around. Serve tracks >= start ascending, then jump to the lowest remaining track and keep ascending. The jump counts as head movement.
